about.title: Rancho Santa Margarita Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Rancho Santa Margarita residents rely on a mix of local clinics and larger Orange County hospital systems for care, and most visits go fine. But when a diagnosis is missed, a surgery goes wrong, or medication is mismanaged, the physical and emotional toll can be significant. California law treats these cases differently than an ordinary injury claim — medical malpractice suits fall under MICRA, which brings specific notice requirements, tight filing windows, and a cap on certain damages. Because a poor result alone doesn't prove negligence, these cases usually require a qualified medical expert to explain what standard of care should have been followed and how it was missed. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects Rancho Santa Margarita patients and families with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened, explain your options, and help you understand whether your situation may qualify for a claim, all without any upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Early

items.title: Deadlines Are Unforgiving
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from discovering the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, to file — missing that window can end a valid claim.

items.title: A 90-Day Notice Comes First
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can be filed, California law requires a formal 90-day notice to the provider, so early legal guidance matters in Rancho Santa Margarita just as much as anywhere else.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Needed
items.desc: Because a bad outcome alone isn't malpractice, a qualified medical expert typically has to establish that the standard of care was breached — an attorney can help arrange that review.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law recognizes that not every complication or disappointing result means a provider was negligent. A valid claim generally requires showing the provider fell below the accepted standard of care and that this deviation caused harm, which is why expert review matters so much.

items.question: How much time do I have to file a claim in Rancho Santa Margarita?
items.answer: Under MICRA, you generally have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but no more than three years from the date of the injury itself. There are limited exceptions, so it's worth having a case reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: Are damages limited in California malpractice cases?
items.answer: California caps certain non-economic damages, though that cap rises each year under current law. Economic damages, like medical bills and lost income, are generally handled separately. An attorney can walk through how this applies to your specific situation.
